items.title: One evolving scene, not slides
items.statement: A presentation is a single evolving diagrammatic scene rendered through an ordered list of named steps (states), rather than a deck of independent slides.

sources.heading: Requirement: Scene step model
sources.quote: A presentation SHALL be one scene rendered through an ordered list of named steps.

sources.heading: What Changes
sources.quote: Model presentations as one evolving diagrammatic scene, not as independent

anchors.met: A spec requirement or scenario, design decision, or proposal scope statement commits that a presentation is one diagram/scene that evolves through an ordered sequence of named or titled steps (states), explicitly as opposed to a deck of independent slides. The contrast with slides may be implied by the model (one scene, many states) rather than stated, and the steps need not be called "steps"; a test-plan-only or passing mention does not count.
anchors.partial: The artifacts commit to one evolving scene moving through ordered states, but the steps have no name, title, or other per-step label, or the single-scene model is hedged (for example, "usually" one scene, or slides with some shared elements).
anchors.missing: No artifact defines the single-evolving-scene model, or it appears only as an open question, in the test plan, or in a passing mention. Contradiction example: each step is defined as its own slide that renders its own independent diagram.

items.title: Step identity, section label, and diagram state

items.intent: Each step is individually identifiable and defines the diagram state shown while it is active.

anchors.met: A requirement, scenario, or design decision defines each step as individually identifiable (a stable id, key, name, or equivalent) and as defining the diagram state shown while that step is active. Any identification mechanism that achieves this is met (for example, a unique slug per step used for jumping and keys), and a section/era label is not required; a near-miss that does not qualify is identifying steps only by array index while saying nothing about the per-step diagram state.
anchors.partial: Each step defines the diagram state shown while it is active, but how steps are individually identified is left unclear, or identity is given only as a mutable position that changes on reordering.
anchors.missing: No artifact says what a step contains, or it appears only as an open question or test-plan detail. Contradiction example: steps carry only narration text and the diagram is computed independently of which step is active.

items.title: Persisting entities morph in place
items.statement: An entity with the same identity in two consecutive steps keeps that identity and, when navigating between the steps, animates in place from its old state (position, size, label, emphasis) to its new state rather than disappearing and reappearing.

anchors.met: A requirement, scenario, or design decision commits that an entity with the same identity in two consecutive steps keeps that identity and animates in place from its old state to its new state, rather than disappearing and reappearing. Either an explicit list of changes (position, size, label, emphasis) or a general statement that any visual state change of a persisting entity animates in place is met; the animation library and identity mechanism need not match any particular implementation.

anchors.missing: Persisting-entity morphing is absent, only an open question, test-plan only, or a passing mention. Contradiction example: each step transition cross-fades the whole diagram out and the next one in, so persisting entities disappear and reappear.

anchors.met: A requirement, scenario, or design decision specifies that entities introduced by a step animate in with a coherent, defined entrance that does not disrupt the continuity of persisting entities, such as newcomers entering only after persisting entities settle. Another mechanism achieving that intent is met (for example, newcomers fading in on a defined stagger overlapping the tail of the morph while persisting entities keep morphing uninterrupted); a near-miss that does not qualify is newcomers popping in instantly or the whole scene re-rendering so existing entities flash.
anchors.partial: New entities have an animated entrance, but its relation to the persisting entities' movement is left unspecified, or continuity of existing entities during the introduction is not addressed.
anchors.missing: Entrance behavior for new entities is absent, only an open question, test-plan only, or a passing mention. Contradiction example: new entities appear instantly at their final positions before the persisting entities have moved, overlapping them.

anchors.missing: Removal of departing entities is absent, only an open question, test-plan only, or a passing mention. Contradiction example: entities accumulate across steps and are never removed when a later step omits them.

items.intent: Successive states of the same diagram keep scene continuity so entities morph rather than the scene being torn down and rebuilt between steps.

anchors.met: A requirement, scenario, or design decision lets successive states of the same diagram keep one persistent scene, so moving between them updates the existing scene with new step data and entities morph rather than the scene being torn down and rebuilt.
